threads.body: The samples do not exercise either target-mismatch branch introduced by the policy. This server span has the wrong method and no `http.route`, so only the generic method-token rule can fire; likewise, no client sample supplies `url.template`. Add cases with the expected method plus a target that differs from an explicit route/template, and assert `http_span_name_format`, so the behavior called out in the PR remains covered.

replies.body:
Addressed in e34195e39c6d028ad3feaa74e6a2975297787524.

Analysis: The fixture now gives the server an explicit route and the client an explicit URL template. Both samples use the expected GET method and a different target, so they reach the target-mismatch rules instead of the generic method-token rule.

Upsides: The tests now cover both target-mismatch branches and protect the route and template comparisons from regressions.

Downsides: The client fixture helper gains one optional argument.
